criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: The introduction excellently details the mission concept and rationale, addressing Australian coral reef monitoring needs. The choice of a single satellite is clearly justified against constellation alternatives, and specific Australian operators and end-users are identified with literature citations.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Mission design is exemplary. Launch vehicle trades, sun-synchronous orbital mechanics, lack of manoeuvres, ground access via Mount Pleasant, data budgeting, and passive drag-sail de-orbiting are thoroughly analysed. Hand calculations perfectly align with STK outputs and software files are clearly documented.

technical_issues.issue: The launch azimuth formula sin(beta) = cos(i)/cos(phi) determines the inertial velocity azimuth; computing the vehicle's actual burnout heading requires correcting for the Earth's tangential surface velocity.

overall: An outstanding, professionally executed preliminary mission design report. Technical calculations and STK simulations are rigorous, consistent, and well-integrated. All requirements and formatting guidelines are met to an exemplary standard.

feedback.summary: You have produced an outstanding, professionally presented mission design for ZYZZsat. Your technical analyses, hand calculations, and STK integrations are rigorous, and your clear justification of mission requirements and critical evaluation of design constraints demonstrate exemplary engineering maturity. Excellent work across all report sections.
next_steps: In Section 2.2, refine the launch azimuth analysis by correcting the inertial azimuth for Earth's tangential surface velocity to determine the vehicle's true burnout heading.
Develop the technology readiness level (TRL) discussions in Section 3 into a concrete risk-mitigation timeline for the optical payload and launch options.
Carry forward this exemplary practice of dual-verifying numerical derivations against software simulations in your future aerospace engineering projects.

criteria.C1: You did an excellent job in Section 1 establishing the operational need for monitoring Great Barrier Reef coral bleaching. You clearly justified the single-satellite architecture over constellations and accurately mapped Australian end-users with strong literature backing. To maintain this Accomplished standard, continue integrating specific stakeholder operational requirements directly into your mission objectives.
criteria.C2: Your mission design in Section 2 is comprehensive, featuring exceptional alignment between your analytical orbital calculations and STK simulations. To refine your calculations to professional fidelity, adjust the launch azimuth equation in Section 2.2 to account for Earth's tangential surface velocity, which differentiates the inertial trajectory from the vehicle's actual burnout heading.
criteria.C3: In Section 3, you provided a mature synthesis of mission outcomes and effectively identified four genuine technical limitations, including launcher readiness and revisit intervals. To sustain this top-tier Accomplished level, ensure future work recommendations outline concrete engineering mitigation pathways and verification milestones for each identified limitation.
criteria.C4: Your presentation was flawless throughout, featuring a concise Executive Summary, cleanly formatted tables, and well-integrated STK figures. Your consistent report structure and accurate IEEE referencing make the document easy to follow. To maintain this standard, continue ensuring all technical figures and tables are explicitly discussed in the main narrative.
